title.narrative: China Funds-in-Trust (Quanzhou) for Capacity-Building on World Heritage in Afric

description.narrative:
The Africa region contains a remarkable variety of natural and cultural heritage that contributes to our understanding of the evolution of both the planet and humankind. To date, the region has 103 properties (56 cultural, 42 natural, and 5 mixed sites) inscribed on the World Heritage List. However, there are 11 countries with no property inscribed on the World Heritage List and hence not represented on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
The Operational Strategy for Priority Africa (2022-2029) adopted by UNESCO’s General Conference at its 41st session not only stresses the imperative need to protect and preserve Africa’s magnificent and diverse cultural and natural heritage but also emphasises the need to reinforce capacity development. In the framework of this strategy, UNESCO has enhanced efforts, in close collaboration with partners, to mobilise extrabudgetary resources to support its Global Priority Africa. Contributing to the Operational Strategy’s Flagship Programme 3, “Fostering cultural heritage and capacity development”, the project aims to reinforce the capacities of Government institutions, experts and professionals of African States Parties in implementing the World Heritage Convention through comprehensive capacity building programmes, especially in preparing nomination dossiers for potential World Heritage sites.
In addition, during the extended 44th session of the World Heritage Committee (Fuzhou (China)/online meeting, 2021), the World Heritage Committee adopted the Fuzhou Declaration, which reiterates the significance of World Heritage protection and international cooperation and calls for closer international cooperation within the framework of multilateralism and increased support for developing countries, especially those in Africa and Small Island Developing States. In line with the Fuzhou Declaration, this project also aims to promote inter-regional experience-sharing by providing training and knowledge exchanges among African and Chinese heritage experts and site managers. This will, therefore, strengthen the capacities of professionals from both sides in tackling global challenges such as climate change, striking a balance between conservation and development, as well as promoting sustainable tourism, etc.
Finally, the project seeks to promote synergies between the UNESCO Culture Conventions for achieving both the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the African Union's Agenda 2063. It also contributes to the implementation of the Regional Action Plan for Africa (2021-2027) adopted by the World Heritage Committee at its Extended 44th session. This project aspires to advance socio-economic development by developing the capacities of African heritage professionals and ensuring linkages between heritage, creative industries and heritage conservation, and contributing to the UN Sustainable Development Goals targets.
The project will contribute to the Operational Strategy for Priority Africa 2022-2029, as well as support the implementation of the 1972 World Heritage Convention, contributing significantly to achieving the five strategic objectives of the Regional Action Plan for Africa (2021-2027) adopted by the World Heritage Committee at its Extended 44th session in 2021 following the 3rd cycle of Periodic Reporting in the Africa Region.
Additionally, this project has clear outputs in alignment with Aspiration 5 (An Africa with a strong cultural identity, common heritage, shared values and ethics) and Aspiration 6 (An Africa whose development is people-driven, relying on the potential of African people, especially its women and youth, and caring for children) of the African Union’s Agenda 2063: The Africa We Want.
The project underscores the development of robust networks between African and Chinese experts and institutions to facilitate sustainable conservation and effective heritage site management. The activities, scheduled between 2024 and 2026, include mentorship programs, capacity-building sessions in Quanzhou, and bi-annual symposiums promoting international cooperation and knowledge exchange. This aligns with UNESCO's broader objectives under the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the African Union's Agenda 2063, fostering a comprehensive approach to cultural and natural heritage preservation and enhancing global and inter-regional collaboration.
The project will be implemented by UNESCO Headquarters (World Heritage Centre and the Africa Department) in coordination with the UNESCO field offices and in close collaboration with the African World Heritage Fund (AWHF), ICCROM and the Advisory Bodies (ICCROM, ICOMOS and IUCN). In line with UNESCO’s Global Priority on Gender Equality, this project will also aim to further women's active participation and empowerment. Gender parity will be one of the main targets in the selection of beneficiary experts and professionals. In addition, to ensure the quality of its implementation, the project will be monitored, and progress will be regularly evaluated by UNESCO (HQ and Field Offices). Annual progress reports will be submitted to the donor, and a final evaluation will be undertaken at the end of the project.
